key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: This framework can help interpret vibrational spectra and diagnose lattice instabilities in perovskite photovoltaic materials, although solar-cell performance gains are not demonstrated.
method: Use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate infrared and Raman spectra.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites.
Relate spectral features to instability symmetry, coupling strength and dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations link slow polar reorientations to very-low-frequency dielectric response and overdamped tilting modes to persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative accuracy metrics or experimental validation, leaving predictive reliability for device-relevant conditions uncertain.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
